sections.html:
The Warren County Register of Deeds is at 109 South Main Street in Warrenton. It serves the public Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 5. Call (252) 257-3265, or mail to P.O. Box 506, Warrenton, NC 27589. The register is an elected position, filled every second year under G.S. 161-1.

Warren is a rural county of about 20,000 people spread over 443 square miles, and one counter covers all of it. A quick call can save you a drive.

Anyone may read what the office holds. Lookups run on names, so a person hunting for a parcel's owner should have a name. With only a street address, call the tax office at (252) 257-4158.

Recording protects the buyer. Under G.S. 47-18, an unrecorded transfer, or a lease longer than three years, cannot beat a lien creditor or a paying purchaser. Whoever registers first stands first.

The office exists so owners can publish their interest in real estate. It also files births that happened in Warren County, marriage licenses and notary oaths, and it files DD-214 papers for retired service members at no cost.

  • The land side takes deeds, mortgages, releases, plats and powers of attorney.
  • Wills live elsewhere, with the courthouse clerk.
  • Liens and judgments: call the clerk at (252) 257-6300.

Warren County follows the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10. Twenty-six dollars buys the first fifteen pages of an ordinary deed and every page after costs four. A mortgage or deed of trust starts at sixty-four dollars for thirty-five pages, with the same four-dollar overage. Filing a release costs nothing.

What each Warren County filing costs
FilingAmount
Ordinary deed$26 plus $4 per page beyond 15
Mortgage or deed of trust$64 plus $4 per page beyond 35
Release of a mortgageNone
Plat$21 a sheet
Certified vital record by mail$10
DD-214 filingNone

Call the office before mailing a package and confirm the figures for your document.

Sellers pay. For each $500 of value, or any leftover part of $500, the stamp is one dollar, handed to the register before the deed is entered.

The county keeps half for its general fund, and the rest goes to the state monthly, less a small allowance. That is the same as $2 per $1,000. The settlement statement shows the exact stamp.

sections.h2: What to line up before you list
sections.html:
Three items come first: matching names, a current tax account and a document that fits the office's format. The register's website carries a recording checklist and a fee page, and staff answer by phone.

  • Changing who is named takes a fresh deed. Use an attorney, then pay the normal filing fee, plus stamp tax where a price is involved.
  • Check the tax account. Each bill is due on September 1 and starts drawing interest after January 5, under G.S. 105-360.
  • Ask the clerk if a lien or judgment sits on the file.
  • Pay with cash, check or money order, since the office does not take cards.

Make two short calls, one to each office, before listing. Ask the register what format your deed needs, and ask the tax office for the current balance and whether any back years are open. Having both answers early means the closing attorney can work from real numbers instead of guesses, and it keeps a surprise from stalling the sale.

sections.h2: Selling rural land and farm tracts
sections.html:
Farm tracts and family land come up often in a county of this size, and such sales may add a survey, plat or easement, each filed separately. A plat is $21 a sheet. Splitting acreage? Learn the register's plat format before the surveyor starts.

A copy of a recorded map is five cents a page (fifty for large maps) and a deed copy is also five cents. The online search shows scanned deeds. Tax maps, parcel numbers and aerial photos come from tax mapping, not here.

Heirs who want to sell should see whether a deed was ever recorded in their names. Estate papers may start at the clerk.

sections.h2: How far back vital records reach
sections.html:
Birth and death certificates run from 1914 to the present. Delayed birth certificates reach back to the late 1800s. Marriage indexes begin in 1867, and marriage bonds and licenses go back to the late 1800s.

  • Certificates, bonds and licenses are filed only for events that took place in Warren County.
  • NC Vital Records in Raleigh holds records for every county in the state and is the place to ask about events elsewhere. Its line is 919.733.3526.
  • Wills are not here. The Warren County clerk of court keeps them.

Heirs selling a Warren County house will find the register useful for the marriage and death side of the family story, while the will itself sits with the clerk. If an owner died in another county, the record will not be in Warren County's files.

Many visitors come for reasons besides land. A marriage license costs sixty dollars, lasts sixty days and is booked by phone. A certified marriage certificate is ten dollars and can be had starting ten days after the ceremony.

A certified vital record goes only to a short list: the person named, a spouse, parents, siblings, children, grandparents, a legal representative, or someone with proof of a legal need. Plain copies are open to all.

New notaries swear in at the counter without an appointment, bringing the notice from the Secretary of State, for a $10 fee. Births outside the county are recorded by NC Vital Records.

sections.h2: Selling a house with liens or repairs
sections.html:
It can be done. Liens and back taxes come out of the price at closing and the releases get recorded. A house that needs work can find a buyer who takes it as it stands, and a cash sale skips lender repair demands.

Start the title work early so both the register's index and the clerk's judgments are checked.

sections.h2: Looking up and paying a tax bill online
sections.html:
The county's property page for the register of deeds links to a combined tool for paying tax bills and searching property record cards. Questions about assessments still go to the tax office.

Keep the bill and the recorded deed together. When a closing is scheduled, the person handling it will want the account number and the book and page of the last recorded deed, and both come from those two lookups.

Your closing attorney collects the signed deed, confirms the payoff of your loan, and files the deed with the register. The stamp tax is paid out of your proceeds before the deed goes on record. Afterward, ask for the recording details, and watch for the release of your old mortgage, which costs nothing to file. If either looks late, phone the office at (252) 257-3265 with the names on the deed.

faqs.q: Is releasing a Warren County mortgage free?
faqs.a: Yes. No fee applies to recording a satisfaction of a mortgage or deed of trust.

faqs.q: Can Warren County staff name a parcel's owner from an address?
faqs.a: No. Staff search by name only, so address-only callers are sent to the tax office.

faqs.q: Does the Warren County deeds office file wills?
faqs.a: No. The clerk of superior court takes wills and estates. The register takes deeds, mortgages, plats, releases, marriage licenses and notary oaths.

faqs.q: Does Warren County charge to record a DD-214?
faqs.a: No. The office files discharge papers for retired military free.

faqs.q: Who answers deed questions in Warren County?
faqs.a: Phone (252) 257-3265, Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 5. The office is at 109 South Main Street, Warrenton.
